topStories.headline: Waxahachie Mother Charged With Capital Murder in Shooting Deaths of Two Sons
topStories.dek: The Ellis County Sheriff's Office arrested a 42-year-old Waxahachie woman Thursday after deputies found her two sons fatally shot inside the family home.
topStories.body:
A Waxahachie mother is facing two counts of capital murder after authorities say she shot and killed her two sons in the early morning hours of Thursday, October 1, according to the Ellis County Sheriff's Office. Deputies were dispatched to a home in the 900 block of Big Sky Drive shortly after 4 a.m. following a 911 call.

Inside the residence, deputies found two males with gunshot wounds. Christopher Scott Pitre, 21, died at the scene. A 15-year-old boy — whose identity authorities have not released — was taken to a hospital in critical condition and later died there.

Colleen Nichole Lemmon, 42, was arrested October 1 in connection with the killings. Sheriff Brad Norman said evidence gathered at the scene led investigators to identify Lemmon as the suspected shooter. Lemmon was also found at the home with injuries described as non-life-threatening. She was booked into the Wayne McCollum Detention Center following hospital treatment, with bond pending arraignment.

The investigation is being conducted by the Ellis County Sheriff's Office. No additional suspects have been named publicly.

topStories.headline: Stampede of Speed Returns Oct. 9–18: Free Downtown Events Kick Off the Fastest 10 Days in Texas
topStories.dek: The NHRA Texas Fall Nationals at Texas Motorplex bring a cattle drive through downtown Waxahachie and a driver Fan Fest at Railyard Park — both free — before championship racing begins.
topStories.body:
The Stampede of Speed, billed as the fastest ten days in Texas, runs October 9–18, 2026, at the historic Texas Motorplex in Ennis, capping NHRA's 75th anniversary season with the fourth of six playoff races in the Countdown to the Championship.

Two free family events take place in downtown Waxahachie. On Friday, October 9 at high noon, a cattle drive winds through downtown to officially launch the festival. On Thursday, October 15, a Fan Fest at Railyard Park gives attendees a chance to meet NHRA and JEGS All-Star drivers, enjoy live music, and collect free autographs — no ticket required for either event.

The Stars of Texas Music Festival, running October 9–11 inside the Motorplex grounds, features three nights of country music, bull riding, drag racing, BBQ, and lantern releases. Ticketed racing events — including JEGS All-Stars qualifying and the NHRA Texas Fall Nationals — run October 14–18, with Race Day and Finals on Sunday, October 18.

Ticket packages range from single-day admissions to full 10-day passes. Information is available at stampedeofspeed.com and the Waxahachie Convention and Visitors Bureau site.

topStories.headline: Farm Heritage Day Returns to Ellis County Rural Heritage Farm This Sunday
topStories.dek: The 145-acre working farm west of Waxahachie opens its gates Sunday, Oct. 4, for a free afternoon of hayrides, live music, hands-on pioneer skills, and farm animals.
topStories.body:
The Ellis County Rural Heritage Farm will hold its annual Farm Heritage Day on Sunday, October 4, from 2 to 5 p.m. at 130 Cunningham Meadows Road in Waxahachie. Admission, activities, demonstrations, and snacks are all free.

This year's program features outdoor games, hayrides, farm animals — including alpacas, cows, chickens, goats, and horses — and living-history demonstrations such as butter churning, treadle sewing, hand laundry, and corn shelling. Live music will be provided by the Lone Star State Dulcimer Society. A special exhibit this year focuses on Rural Free Delivery, exploring how early mail service connected rural communities much as online delivery does today.

Hands-on activities for children and families are hosted by the 4-H and Girl Scouts, and educational displays will be presented by the Ellis County Historical Commission, the Indian Trail Chapter of Master Naturalists, the American Red Cross, and several other community partners. The restored 1913 McKinney-Aday Farmhouse will be open for tours.

The farm is located approximately two miles west of Waxahachie on FM 66. Turn south at the flashing yellow light onto Cunningham Meadows Road. Free water is provided by AgTexas; snacks are provided by H-E-B while supplies last. Vendors will also be on site selling items for purchase.

moreNews.headline: Voter Registration Deadline for November Election Is Monday, Oct. 5
moreNews.body: Monday, October 5, 2026, is the last day for Ellis County residents to register to vote — or update their voter record — for the November 3, 2026, General and Special Elections. The deadline applies to both mail and in-person registration. Early voting runs October 19–30 at county vote centers. Sample ballots and polling location listings are available at elliscountytx.gov.

moreNews.headline: Global High School Awarded $100,000 DART Foundation Grant
moreNews.body: Waxahachie Global High School received a $100,000 grant from the DART Foundation as part of the foundation's Closing the Gap project, according to an announcement posted September 18, 2026, on the school's website. Global High, located at 600 W. 2nd St., is a T-STEM Early College High School within Waxahachie ISD serving students in grades 9–12.
